findings.title: resolveLinkKind's per-LANE link authority — the tab's whole defence against a policy-gate row wearing a held draft's review link — is asserted by no test
findings.reason: Rewriting the lane key to a category key (`source === 'held_draft'` -> `category === 'unsafe_content'`) leaves all 23 live-DB cases green. Only ONE integration case asserts `linkKind` at all, and its three fixtures cannot separate the two rules: its `held_draft` rows all carry `unsafe_content`, and its only non-`held_draft` subject-bearing fixture is unresolvable, so both rules return null. The promised collision test (intake title 47) lives on RestraintReport, which is handed a `linkKind` and cannot detect a wrong one — RestraintReport.tsx:63-65 says so itself. Add a live-DB case seeding a `policy_gate_held` row with category `unsafe_content` and a RESOLVING response subject, asserting `linkKind` is null beside a `held_draft` row that resolves to 'review'.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: for a `policy_gate_held` row with category `unsafe_content` and a resolving `responses` subject, the original returns null and the mutant returns 'review' — exactly the wrong-link collision migration 116's CHECK C1 makes representable (both lanes take subject_type 'response'). Not an unexecuted branch: line 122 is evaluated for every entry the read returns, in every one of the 23 cases.

findings.title: the LOCATION entry arm's upper window bound is asserted by no test
findings.reason: Deleting `AND r.occurred_at <= ${windowEnd}` from the location arm leaves all 23 cases green. The promised bound test (intake title 19) exercises the ACCOUNT arm and the footnote only. read.ts:233-235 states the bound exists because `occurred_at` is writer-supplied and a clock-skewed row must not appear after the range the tab prints — that is true of a location view too. Extend title 19, or add its location-scope twin.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: a location-scope read of a row dated after `windowEnd` is included by the mutant and excluded by the original; the suite proves the same predicate matters on the account arm. Not unexecuted: the location arm runs in eight cases, including the two that pin its scope predicate.

findings.title: the account entry arm's LOWER window bound is asserted by no test — nothing proves the selected window filters at its opening edge
findings.reason: Deleting `AND r.occurred_at >= ${windowStart}` from the account arm leaves all 23 cases green. Every seeded Refusal is minutes old while `windowStart` is at most 90 days back, so no fixture can distinguish a bounded window from an unbounded one. This is the predicate that makes '30d' mean 30 days, and the same clamp E13 exists to move. Seed a row older than `windowStart` (e.g. `NOW() - interval '45 days'`) in a 30d read and assert it is absent.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: without the predicate an account read returns the entire retained ledger regardless of the selected window, and the summary sentence would then name a range it did not query. Not unexecuted: the account arm's WHERE clause runs in roughly twenty of the 23 cases.

findings.title: the `subject_resolves` business correlation — read.ts's stated cross-location guard — is asserted by no test
findings.reason: Removing `AND resp.business_id = r.business_id` from BOTH subqueries leaves all 23 cases green. read.ts:253-256 sells that clause as 'stronger than a bare id match either way: a response belonging to another location cannot resolve', and it is what stops a `held_draft` row linking to a sibling location's review. Every fixture seeds the response under the Refusal's own business, so the correlation is never exercised. Seed a `held_draft` Refusal on location A whose `subject_id` is a response owned by sibling location B and assert `linkKind` is null.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: with a cross-location subject the original yields subject_resolves false (linkKind null) and the mutant yields true (a 'review' link into another location's review). Not unexecuted: the correlated EXISTS is evaluated for every returned row in all 23 cases; only the discriminating DATA is missing.

findings.title: RestraintContent's success path is rendered by no test, so the `scope` prop that picks which owner-facing sentence appears is unwired-untested
findings.reason: All six RestraintContent cases return at `if (panel) return panel` — one reads the source as text, the other five stub a pending or failing fetch. Inverting the `scope` ternary changes nothing, because the JSX is never constructed. The prop decides between 'This is your whole account…' and 'This is one location…' — the D3 disclosure CONTEXT.md requires — and RestraintReport.tsx:23-28 explicitly refuses to derive it, on the grounds that passing it is safer. Nothing proves it is passed correctly. Add one case with a resolving fetch that asserts the report renders and that a non-'all' scope produces the location sentence.

findings.title: the null-`coverageStart` branch is rendered by no test, though three documents call it load-bearing
findings.reason: No fixture in the 17-case suite sets `coverageStart: null`, so replacing `return null` with a rendered sentence stays green. `businesses.created_at` really is nullable — confirmed against the live schema, not just migration 001 — and CONTEXT.md's Coverage start bullet, read.ts:372-375 and coverageLine's own comment all state that the tab must OMIT the line rather than name a date it does not have. The read's matching behaviour (a null coverage start also leaves `windowStart` unclamped) is equally unasserted. Add a `{ coverageStart: null }` override asserting no 'We have been watching since' text, and a live-DB case with `businesses.created_at = NULL`.

findings.title: the ADR 0023 redaction assertion on the component is an absence-of-substring proxy that cannot fail for the reason it claims
findings.reason: `expect(container.textContent).not.toMatch(/reason|draft|moderat/i)` stands in for 'shows no draft text, review text or moderation reason'. It cannot catch a real leak — the DTO carries no prose field, so there is nothing for the component to render — while it CAN redden on an innocuous copy change: any future category sentence or link label containing 'draft' or 'reason' fails it. That is the absence-of-tag proxy shape (passes while the bug exists, fails on the fix). Replace it with a positive closure: assert the row's rendered text set is exactly {formatted date} plus the optional link label, so any added field fails whatever it is spelled.

findings.title: the routed Restraint page has no covering test in any project
findings.reason: Direction B: `page.tsx` is a new production file with no Vitest importer and no e2e spec, so nothing proves the route exists, mounts `RestraintContent`, or pulls in `restraint.css` — while `AnalyticsTabs` now links to it from three surfaces (AnalyticsContent's state panel, AnalyticsAggregateView, AnalyticsPerLocationView) and would produce a 404 if the page were lost. It is the thinnest possible hunk (a `force-dynamic` export and a two-line component), so accept-risk is a defensible adjudication — but the rule records an uncovered production hunk as P1, and this is one.

findings.title: the singular arms of three owner-facing count phrases are rendered by existing fixtures and asserted by nothing
findings.reason: Mutating `'thing'`->`'things'`, `'time'`->`'times'` and `'1 archived location'`->`'1 archived locations'` together leaves all 17 cases green, so '1 things we chose not to do' and '1 times' would ship. Two of the three arms are actually EXECUTED by the single-entry link fixtures — they are rendered and simply not asserted. On a surface whose own header says 'THIS COMPONENT OWNS EVERY OWNER-FACING SENTENCE' and whose comment calls the words the contract, the plural forms are pinned and the singular forms are not. Recorded, not blocking: no behaviour beyond copy is at risk.

findings.title: docs/directory.md’s new `read.ts` row overstates trap (d): two of the three link kinds ARE keyed on the Refusal category
findings.reason: The row says 'link authority is the server-resolved `linkKind`, never the **Refusal category**'. read.ts:123-124 keys `auto-approval` on `category === 'autonomy_paused'` and `contacts` on `category === 'no_permission'`; only the review link is lane-keyed. read.ts:113-115 states the distinction correctly ('The two category-keyed links carry no subject and are safe to key that way'). The directory row's trailing clause carries the real reason, so a reader who finishes the sentence is not misled — which is why this is recorded rather than raised as a false claim. Narrow it to 'the REVIEW link is never keyed on the Refusal category'. Every other citation in the change resolves: flags.ts:3, vocabulary.ts:30-33, DashboardStatePanel.tsx:61 at the fork, console.css's section-enter-6 ceiling, DESIGN.md § Tabs (line 530), migration 116's C1/C3, ReviewsTabs, CardViewTabs.tsx:15, BatchReport.tsx:218, VAL-LOC-044 (13 hits, 8 files), and both nullability claims verified against the live schema.

findings.title: restraint.css ships three rule sets for elements no component renders
findings.reason: `.rst-group-link` (:112, :120, and a reduced-motion rule at :179), `.rst-row-ago` (:157) and `.rst-error-body` (:184) match nothing: a repo-wide grep over .ts/.tsx finds no emitter. `.rst-error-body` in particular is the fingerprint of a local error card the ticket deliberately replaced with the shared state panel, so this is an incomplete cleanup rather than forward-looking CSS. Sibling search recorded: every other `rst-` class the component emits IS styled (`.rst-summary` and `.rst-group` intentionally carry no rules of their own — they compose with `.card`).

findings.title: five new production files were added with no docs/directory.md row, and CI cannot see it
findings.reason: `ci:directory-map` passes (586 files) because it only enforces `worker/` and `src/lib/`, and `src/lib/refusals/read.ts` correctly got its row. But the map also maintains per-file rows for `src/components/` (including `dashboard/AgentTeamStrip.tsx`, this ticket's own cited precedent) and for route-colocated app files (including `dashboard/requests/requests.css`). RestraintContent.tsx, RestraintReport.tsx, AnalyticsTabs.tsx, the restraint `page.tsx` and `restraint.css` have none. Non-blocking — the CLAUDE.md rule scopes the requirement to the two enforced roots — but the code map other agents read is now incomplete for this feature.
